title: Let the sheet do the maths
goal: Spot the repetitive sheet work you can safely hand to a formula — and the judgement you keep.

blocks.title: The gradebook that never ends
blocks.body:
It's the end of term. You're re-totalling the same gradebook by hand, cell by cell, checking attendance percentages on a calculator.

Here's the quiet truth: the maths part isn't your job. A sheet can do it in one line — and it never makes an arithmetic slip. Let's take that work off your plate in about 4 minutes.

blocks.title: Say it in plain words, get a formula
blocks.body:
You don't need to know spreadsheet syntax. You describe the task in plain words — "add up columns B to F for each student and give a percentage" — and AI writes the formula and the step-by-step for you.

You then paste it into your own Google Sheet or Excel and check it on one row you already know the answer to. AI does the typing; you stay the checker.
blocks.goDeeper: AI can't see your live sheet, so it works from what you tell it: your column letters and what each holds. The clearer you name your columns, the better the formula — and you always verify it on a known row before trusting the whole sheet.

blocks.question: Tap every task that's safe to hand to a formula (and leave the ones that need your judgement).

options.text: Add up marks across five tests into a total
Turn attendance counts into a percentage
Decide whether a borderline 79% becomes a B+ or an A
Judge why a bright student suddenly dropped marks

blocks.explanation: Totals, percentages and pass/fail flags are pure maths — hand them over gladly. But a borderline grade or the reason behind a dip needs your knowledge of the child. Automate the arithmetic; keep the judgement.

blocks.question: How clear are you now on what's safe to automate and what to keep?
